```{r} #| label: setup #| message: false #| warning: false #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(scales) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) # fonts ---- library(extrafont) library(sysfonts) source("_common.R") # use font showtext::showtext_auto() # set theme ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_netware( base_size = 15)) ``` ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"} ## Theme: `theme_netware()` Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_netware()`, built from Novell NetWare 2.0 boxes: a NetWare red background with white text, a maroon frame, maroon, red, rose, and blush marks, and a Gill Sans title. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (continuous) variable** **✅ a categorical variable** ::: ```{r} #| label: full_code_display #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '60%' #| out-width: '60%' #| fig-align: right library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) set.seed(1990) netware_offices <- tibble( year = c("1990", "1994", "1998"), mean_nodes = c(22, 24, 27)) |> tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "office") |> mutate(nodes = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_nodes, sd = 2.5)), lan_size = if_else(nodes >= 25, "25 or more", "Under 25")) |> select(year, office, nodes, lan_size) labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years", x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) + geom_bar() ggp2_bar_ovrlp + labs_bar_ovrlp ``` :::: ## Description Overlapping bar graphs display multiple variables on the same graph. Bars overlap instead of being placed side by side. Bars are often made partially transparent to aid visibility. A legend is essential to distinguish between data. In `ggplot2`, we can build overlapping bar graphs using the `fill` argument in `geom_bar()` or `geom_col()` ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"} Install packages. ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: pkg_code_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: hide library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(tidyr) # for uncount() ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"} Novell NetWare was the most popular network operating system of the early 90s, and office LANs grew as more desks got a PC and a network card. We'll simulate the number of workstations on the LAN for 24 offices in 1990, 1994, and 1998. Each year gets its own average LAN size (`mean_nodes`), `tidyr::uncount()` creates one row per office, and `rnorm()` draws each office's workstation count, rounded to a whole workstation. We'll also flag whether each office ran 25 workstations or more (`lan_size`). Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 72 offices every time you run the code below. ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: data_code_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true set.seed(1990) netware_offices <- tibble( year = c("1990", "1994", "1998"), mean_nodes = c(22, 24, 27)) |> tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "office") |> mutate(nodes = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_nodes, sd = 2.5)), lan_size = if_else(nodes >= 25, "25 or more", "Under 25")) |> select(year, office, nodes, lan_size) glimpse(netware_offices) ``` ::: ## Distribution Overlapping bars only overlap when groups share values. Three years with very different LAN sizes would sit side by side with no stacking at all, and three years with the same LAN size would stack into a single pile. How much the bars overlap depends on how far apart the years' averages are compared to how much offices vary within a year. Below we'll move from the offices, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the first six offices from 1990. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_values_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true head(netware_offices, 6) ``` ::: These offices ran between 20 and 26 workstations. The summary below shows each year's mean, standard deviation, and range. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_summary_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true netware_offices |> group_by(year) |> summarise( mean = mean(nodes), sd = sd(nodes), min = min(nodes), max = max(nodes)) ``` ::: Each year's range covers 8 to 11 workstations, but the means are only about 2 to 5 workstations apart. So the ranges overlap, which is what puts more than one color in the same bar. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: The overlapping bar graph below stacks the offices from all three years at each LAN size. The dashed lines mark the average LAN size we gave each year in `rnorm()`. The 1990 offices sit mostly on the left, the 1998 offices mostly on the right, and the 1994 offices land in the middle, sharing bars with both. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) + geom_bar() + geom_vline(xintercept = c(22, 24, 27), color = c("#69100A", "#A91E28", "#B3575A"), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) + labs(x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each year's LAN size comes from its own [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) with a shared standard deviation: $$ X_{y} \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_y, \sigma = 2.5), \quad \mu_{1990} = 22, \; \mu_{1994} = 24, \; \mu_{1998} = 27 $$ The overlap depends on the distance between two means measured in standard deviations. The 1990 and 1998 means are $(27 - 22) / 2.5 = 2$ standard deviations apart, and the 1994 and 1998 means are only $(27 - 24) / 2.5 = 1.2$ apart. One way to put a number on that overlap is to pick a random office from each year and ask how often the "smaller" year wins: $$ P(X_{1994} > X_{1998}) = \Phi\left(\frac{24 - 27}{2.5\sqrt{2}}\right) \approx 0.20 $$ So a 1994 office runs more workstations than a 1998 office about 20% of the time, while a 1990 office does so only about 8% of the time. Try moving the three means in `mean_nodes` closer together and the bars stack into a single colorful pile. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map `nodes` to the `x` and `year` to `fill` - Add the `geom_bar()` layer ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_bar_ovrlp #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years", x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) + geom_bar() ggp2_bar_ovrlp + labs_bar_ovrlp ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ```{r} #| label: create_graph_bar_ovrlp #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years", x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) + geom_bar() ggp2_bar_ovrlp + labs_bar_ovrlp ``` ## More info - Overlapping bar graphs can also be built with `geom_col()`. - `geom_bar()` has additional options for arranging overlapping bars. We can set the `position` argument to `"dodge"` or `"dodge2"`, depending on how we'd like the data displayed. ### `geom_col()`
To build an overlapping bar graph with `geom_col()`, we need to create a column with the counts for `nodes` and `year` in the dataset. - Create the `netware_col` data: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: netware_col #| eval: true #| echo: true netware_col <- netware_offices |> count(year, nodes, name = "Offices") ``` ::: - Map the counts to the `y` axis, `nodes` to the `x` axis, and `year` to `fill` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: data_code_bar_netware_col #| eval: true #| echo: true #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_col_ovrlp <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "built with 'geom_col()'", x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_col_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_col, mapping = aes(y = Offices, x = nodes, fill = year)) + geom_col() ggp2_col_ovrlp + labs_col_ovrlp ``` ::: Compare the two graphs below: ```{r} #| label: compare_bar_col #| eval: true #| echo: false #| layout-nrow: 1 ggp2_bar_ovrlp + labs_bar_ovrlp ggp2_col_ovrlp + labs_col_ovrlp ``` ### `dodge`
::: {.column-margin} - *`position = "dodge"` preserves the vertical position of a geom while adjusting the horizontal position* - *`"dodge"` requires the grouping variable to be be specified in the global or `⁠geom_`⁠ layer* ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"} We'll use the `lan_size` column, which splits offices into those with 25 workstations or more and those with fewer. ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: netware_dodge #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false count(netware_offices, lan_size, year) ``` ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map `lan_size` to the `x` and `year` to `group` and `fill` - Inside the `geom_bar()` function, set `position` to `"dodge"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_dodge #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_bar_dodge <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "position = 'dodge'", x = "LAN size", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_bar_dodge <- ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = lan_size, group = year, fill = year)) + geom_bar( position = "dodge") ggp2_bar_dodge + labs_bar_dodge ``` ::: ### `dodge2`
- Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map `lan_size` to `x` and `year` to `fill` - Inside `geom_bar()`, set `position` to `"dodge2"` ::: {.column-margin} - *`"dodge2"` works without a grouping variable in a layer* - *`"dodge2"` works with bars and rectangles* - *`"dodge2"` is useful for arranging graphs with variable widths.* ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: create_graph_dodge2 #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_bar_dodge2 <- labs( title = "Novell NetWare", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "position = 'dodge2'", x = "LAN size", y = "Offices", fill = "Year") ggp2_bar_dodge2 <- ggplot(data = netware_offices, aes(x = lan_size, fill = year)) + geom_bar( position = "dodge2") ggp2_bar_dodge2 + labs_bar_dodge2 ``` ::: Compare the two graphs below: ```{r} #| label: compare_bars #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 ggp2_bar_dodge + labs_bar_dodge ggp2_bar_dodge2 + labs_bar_dodge2 ```
